title: The codegree conjecture for spanning spheres in uniform hypergraphs
statement:
Let $rgeq 2$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $r$-graph on $n>r$ vertices. For a set of $r-1$ vertices, its codegree is the number of edges containing it, and a **tight component** is an equivalence class under the transitive closure of the relation that two edges satisfy when they meet in $r-1$ vertices.

**Higher-dimensional spanning-sphere conjecture.** If $\mathcal{H}$ comprises a single tight component and every set $Z$ of $r-1$ vertices contained in an edge of $\mathcal{H}$ is contained in at least $n/2$ edges, then $\mathcal{H}$ contains a spanning copy of the $(r-1)$-dimensional sphere $\mathbb{S}^{r-1}$.

This conjecture is motivated by a construction showing that a spanning tight component alone does not force a spanning surface. It predicts a codegree threshold of $1/2$, independent of the dimension, but no resolution is supplied.
source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos, John Haslegrave, Richard Montgomery and Bhargav Narayanan, “Spanning surfaces in 3-graphs”, arXiv:1808.06864 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.06864

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2018). “We shall resist the temptation to list further open problems of this kind here, although we would certainly be very interested to see more results of this nature.”
